paper_title: Hot Spot Identification and System Parameterized Thermal Modeling for Multi-Core Processors Through Infrared Thermal Imaging

extraction.paper_title: Hot Spot Identification and System Parameterized Thermal Modeling for Multi-Core Processors Through Infrared Thermal Imaging

scenario.description: Intel i5-3337U dual-core processor imaged with a rear-cooled IR thermography setup (FLIR A325sc, 50 um/pixel). 18 heat-sources were identified via DCT filtering, Laplacian and K-means. An LSTM model predicts the temperature of each heat-source from 80 PCM performance metrics. Table I gives RMSE per heat-source (2.04 to 2.57 C), and Fig. 10 compares predicted and measured temperature for heat-source #1 over about 8 minutes.
scenario.architecture: Intel i5-3337U, 2 cores with 2 threads per core, rear-mounted Peltier thermo-electric cooling with liquid-cooled hot side, front side exposed to the IR camera
scenario.workload: Mixed realistic workloads over 52 minutes at 60 Hz (187200 samples): idling, word processing, data compression, compute-intensive and memory-intensive tasks
scenario.operating_point: Observed temperature range 58.73 C to 101.35 C. Frequency, voltage and instruction count are model inputs; no single steady power or frequency is published.

original_setup.solver: No numerical thermal solver. Temperatures are measured with a FLIR A325sc IR camera (320x240, 60 Hz, 50 um/pixel, microscope lens) on an Intel i5-3337U. Heat sources are located by 2D DCT noise filtering, a 2D discrete Laplacian and K-means clustering. A trained LSTM predicts temperatures. A COMSOL simulation (Fig. 3, PDF p.3) validates only the Laplacian heat-source identification idea. (PDF pp.2-5)
original_setup.optimizer: Neural-network training for 100 epochs with 60 timesteps, 20% dropout and a 60/15/25 train/validation/test split. The optimizer algorithm is not named. K-means with the elbow criterion selects k. No design or placement optimizer is used. (PDF pp.4-5)
original_setup.controller: None. No thermal or power controller is implemented. The paper motivates DVFS and thermal management only as future uses. Rear-mounted Peltier cooling with a liquid-cooled hot side is a measurement fixture, not a controller. (PDF pp.2,6)
original_setup.benchmark: Intel i5-3337U, 2 cores and 2 threads per core, run under mixed real workloads (idle, word processing, data compression, compute-intensive and memory-intensive tasks). 187200 samples at 60 Hz (52 min), each with 80 Intel PCM metrics and 18 heat-source temperatures. (PDF pp.2,4-5)

thermal_observable.unit: degC (RMSE of predicted vs measured heat-source temperature)
thermal_observable.location: 18 identified heat-sources on the i5-3337U die surface, imaged by IR. Table I gives per-source RMSE, and Fig. 10 shows heat-source #1 (THS#1).
thermal_observable.aggregation: Per-heat-source RMSE of the LSTM prediction on the held-out 25% test set. The range across sources is 2.04 degC (HS#11) to 2.57 degC (HS#10). No single scalar is selected, so value is null. The observed dynamic range is 58.73 to 101.35 degC. (PDF p.6, Table I)

physical_mismatches.reason: No floorplan geometry is published (no block x, y, width, height), and no per-block power in watts. The 18 heat-source centroids lack named blocks and dimensions, and the paper explicitly says it does not use the processor floorplan. A Studio 2D steady-state model cannot be built from the paper's facts, and this is essential.

Cooling mismatch: the experiment uses a rear-mounted Peltier/thermo-electric cooler with a liquid-cooled hot side, and the die front is exposed bare to the IR camera. There is no heat sink or package lid in the measurement, which differs from a typical heat-sink-based chip stack.

Transient and workload mismatch: the result is a dynamic, workload-driven LSTM prediction (60 Hz time series over 52 minutes). No steady-state power map or single operating point is published, so a steady 2D solve does not correspond to the paper's observable.

Solver mismatch: the paper uses data-driven LSTM regression and image processing, not a finite-difference or finite-element thermal solver. Only a simple COMSOL validation of the Laplacian idea is mentioned. A Studio solver would not reproduce the RMSE metric.

The paper reports no 3D stacking, interposer, chiplet, optimizer or reliability evaluation. Reliability (EM, BTI, HCI) is mentioned only as motivation. The die is a single commercial processor, so interposer and placement-optimizer features of the Studio package are not applicable.

studio_assumptions: No paper-derived floorplan exists, so any Studio run would use a separate illustrative 2D placement with generated coordinates, kept distinct from paper facts.

Any illustrative run would use the Studio's bundled default package and material assumptions (default die, TIM, heat spreader and boundary conditions). Their values were not supplied in the packet and are not paper-derived.
Total chip power cannot be split across blocks because the paper publishes no power or splitting rule. Any power would be a one-row illustrative trace, not paper data.
Temperatures from an illustrative Studio run must not be compared numerically to the paper's RMSE (2.04 to 2.57 degC) or temperature range.

methods.note: The text claims about the IR setup, DCT, Laplacian, K-means and LSTM are supported on pp.2-5. The experiment block labels the work custom_2d_steady with an empty floorplan and empty power. That contradicts the extraction's own steady_2d_relevant=false and the essential physical_mismatches, because the paper's method is measured IR imaging plus a transient LSTM, not a 2D steady solve.

code.note: The packet assets list is empty and artifact_search_status is checked_no_links. No code, repository, trained LSTM weights or analysis scripts are supplied. Reference [22] is only the Intel PCM tool URL, which is not evidence of reproducible code.

parameters.note: The reported scalars are supported by pdftotext: Table I RMSE values (HS#1 2.36, HS#10 2.57, HS#11 2.04), the 58.73-101.35 C range, 50 um/pixel, 60 Hz, 18 sources, 187200 samples, 52 min, 80 metrics, and the LSTM layout of 100/80/60 neurons plus an 18-neuron dense layer with 20% dropout, 100 epochs, 60 timesteps and a 60/15/25 split. No block x/y/width/height, die size, per-block watts, Peltier setpoint, material properties, or LSTM optimizer and loss are published, so the parameters needed for any 2D scenario are absent.

assessment.summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable, and Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped). The gate reports simulation_allowed=false, input_gate_pass=false, scientific_gate_pass=false, and comparison_valid=false. The scenario is a custom 2D steady experiment type, but it has no blocks and no power_w object. A custom 2D steady run has no transient trace, while the paper's observable is a 60 Hz, 52-minute workload-driven LSTM prediction on an Intel i5-3337U. The paper reports per-heat-source RMSE of 2.04 to 2.57 degC (HS#11 lowest, HS#10 highest, HS#1 at 2.36 degC) and an observed range of 58.73 to 101.35 degC. These are data-driven prediction errors, not outputs of a thermal solver, so a steady 2D solve would not correspond to them. There is no pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace asset, no bundled EV6/GCC adaptation, and no generated placement. No source commit exists and no input.flp or input.ptrace was produced. No numerical comparison is made, since the Studio produced no temperatures and the location, aggregation, regime, and boundary assumptions do not match. Only qualitative sensitivity is discussed. The paper's cooling is a rear Peltier with a liquid-cooled hot side and a bare die facing the IR camera, whereas a Studio run would use default package assumptions. The result is a not-applicable verdict, and it must not be read as replication or validation of the paper.
